title: Monotonicity analysis and the boundaries of avoidable coordination
text: Ju applies the distributed systems CALM theorem to organizational tasks, demonstrating that coordination mechanisms are required for correctness only when tasks are non-monotonic (where new information can invalidate prior conclusions). Across 65 APQC enterprise workflows, 48 (74%) were classified as monotonic and provably executable without coordination, with non-monotonic workflows clustering around shared finite resources such as budgets, headcounts, and physical capacity. Replicating across 13,417 O*NET occupational tasks yielded a 42% monotonic rate.
qualification: Academic preprint under review. Multi-agent simulations confirmed the theoretical predictions; the 65 APQC enterprise workflows and 13,417 O*NET occupational tasks were classified using the monotonicity framework. Crucially, the author notes that monotonicity guarantees only computational correctness without synchronization, not qualitative coherence, strategic alignment, or task quality.
